Private Flagstaff Snow Day Tour from Phoenix and Scottsdale

Scottsdale Sprinters runs a private Flagstaff Snow Day tour from Phoenix and Scottsdale as one vehicle and one chauffeur held for a 12-hour day: the group is driven up, waited on at every confirmed stop, and driven home. The published window is 10-12 hours and it bills 10 of them, so the day starts at $1,250 in the Luxury SUV (Suburban) and the 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter is $1,450 before 8% tax — roughly $104 a seat with 14 aboard. Below: the row's own 7 steps, what this page will and will not promise about the day itself, which vehicle fits, and how the quote is built. Reservations: (623) 986-6339.

Last updated: September 18, 2026

What is a private Flagstaff day tour from Phoenix and Scottsdale?

It is the whole vehicle and one chauffeur held for a 12-hour day up the mountain and back, not a seat on somebody else's coach. 5 vehicles are offered for it: the day starts at $1,250 in the smallest cabin and tops out at $2,250, every figure quoted in writing first. Scottsdale Sprinters sells the transport and nothing that happens at the stops. Your group decides who is aboard and how the booked hours are spent; the chauffeur drives, parks, waits, and brings everyone home — the part that matters most on a route nobody wants to drive twice in one day. Per head the arithmetic is plainer than it looks. The 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter splits $1,450 across its seats, about $104 each; the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) splits $2,250 across 29, about $78. Those are the current published hourly rates carried across this day, never a fare per person.

How does the day work, from pickup to the drive home?

The tour publishes 7 steps and states the window as 10-12 hours. 3 of them are written as conditional on purpose, because what is open on your date is decided by the people who run it rather than by a transportation booking. That is the row's own list, word for word, and here are the conditional steps in full: "Drive to Flagstaff using the route approved for current conditions", "Confirmed Snowbowl or Flagstaff activity if currently operating" and "Optional: Lowell Observatory visit". None is dropped from a quote and none is turned into a promise. Together they are the honest shape of this day: a confirmed vehicle around an unconfirmed mountain. The steps that are not conditional are the ones this site controls: "Morning pickup" is set backward from whatever you have reserved, and "Return to Scottsdale" closes the row because the vehicle is yours for the whole window. What does the tour publish as the day out?

The row names 6 highlights, and they are the only ones this page will name: Arizona Snowbowl, Downtown Flagstaff, Historic Route 66, Pine forest scenery, Mountain dining, Snow activities. Each is somewhere the vehicle can wait while the group is out of it. Two of those are run by other people, and the row is explicit about who decides whether they happen at all. That answer is reprinted whole further down this page, and the official sources behind it are cited at the foot of the article; this page lifts no price, status or timetable from them. The rest are places you walk into and out of at your own pace, in a town small enough that a group on foot stays together. Nothing here promises a named stop will be open on your date.

Which vehicle fits the group, and what does the day cost?

Group size decides it. This tour offers 5 vehicles, and every row below prices the identical 12-hour day: the published hourly rate times 10 billable hours, because 12 requested hours earn 2 free hours on the standard ladder, against each vehicle's own 4-hour minimum. Up to 6 travellers the Luxury SUV (Suburban) runs the day for $1,250, the row's first recommendation and the smallest cabin of the 5 offered. The Executive Black Sprinter and Executive White Sprinter share a rate at $145 an hour and seat 14 each. Past 14 seats it is the Mini Bus (24 Pax), then the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax), which seats 29 and is the dearest line here at $2,250. The per-seat column divides the day total by seated capacity — friends splitting one fare. It is why the cheapest seat and the cheapest day are different vehicles: the Luxury SUV (Suburban) is the least expensive booking at $1,250, while the Mini Bus (24 Pax) carries the cheapest seat at $77. What is in the fare, and what is not?

A 12-hour day in the 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter is $1,450 before 8% tax — $145 an hour across 10 billable hours, roughly $104 a seat split 14 ways. The least expensive vehicle on the list runs the same day for $1,250. Three rules build every number: the day is priced by the hour against each vehicle's published minimum, hours above the ladder's rungs earn free hours, and 8% tax is the only addition. 50% is taken today by card, the balance 48 hours before pickup. What the fare excludes is everything the row hands to somebody else: "Check Arizona Snowbowl's current equipment, ticket, and operating policies directly. Guests arrange and pay rentals or lift access themselves unless the written quote expressly includes a listed item." Lunch is a stop rather than a service — "No eating or food inside the vehicle. Drinks are fine; snacks wait for the next stop."

How far is Flagstaff from the Valley?

1 figure, and it is not ours: the Downtown Flagstaff service-area guide already publishes the distance to Phoenix Sky Harbor International as 145 miles, and this page reads that number out of the same file rather than restating it. No drive time is published anywhere on this site. Why no drive time: the only honest one is the one the route takes on the day, and that is answered at checkout by the Directions API for your real addresses rather than by a sentence written in advance. What is published instead is the window the booking buys — 10-12 hours — with the travelling inside it rather than on top of it. That is also why the day is priced by the hour. A charter buys time, so a longer stop or a re-routed approach costs nothing extra as long as it fits the window you booked; a longer window is re-quoted before the date.

What has to be confirmed before the date?

Everything that is not the vehicle. The row publishes 3 answers on this, and all 3 point the same way: the people who run the mountain and the roads decide what your day contains, and this site confirms the transportation around whatever they tell you. On whether the day can be promised at all: "No. Snow and mountain conditions vary by date. Check Arizona Snowbowl's current operating report before departure, and treat any snow activity as optional until conditions and tickets are confirmed." On the roads, the row answers in two sentences from two places: "Arizona Department of Transportation advises winter travelers to prepare for snow, ice, and freezing conditions and check AZ511 for current road and weather conditions. Bring appropriate layers and treat every activity as conditional until access and operating status are confirmed." The first summarises the state's guidance, linked at the foot of this article. The second is this site's rule, not the state's.

Who is this day for, and what should we bring?

Groups — and that is as far as this page will go, because the row names no audience. The only honest description is the shape of the booking: 1 vehicle, 1 chauffeur, 12 hours, and a party between 6 and 29 people. What the booking is good at follows from that shape rather than from a customer list. Everyone leaves and arrives together, the cabin is the group's locker while you are out of it, and nobody drives home at the end of a long day. Bags have a published cap per vehicle rather than a house rule: the Luxury SUV (Suburban) takes 10, the Executive Black Sprinter 40, and the 1 unit without an owner-confirmed number has its fit confirmed in writing instead of guessed. Oversized or rented equipment is confirmed in writing. The chauffeur is a resource: "Ask your chauffeur for anything. Stops, temperature, volume, a photo. Really."

Where can the day start, and how is it quoted?

Pickup is a street address in any of the 10 metro cities with a published service-area page, not a zone or a depot. Reserving takes 3 things — the date, the number of people and one address — plus the confirmations for anything you have already reserved. The published service areas are Scottsdale, Phoenix, Paradise Valley, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Glendale, Cave Creek and San Tan Valley. One pickup address for the whole party keeps a group together at the start of a day that begins early and ends late. Every figure here is today's published table; the quote you act on is the written one, naming the vehicle, the hours, the 8% tax and the 50% deposit. Call Scottsdale Sprinters on (623) 986-6339, or send those 3 things and request a current quote.
